hooks.prompt:
A file was just modified. Hook input: $ARGUMENTS

Look at the tool_input.file_path field.

First, skip silently (do nothing) if the modified file:
- is inside docs/, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, src/execsql/data/execsql.conf.template
- is inside .claude/, .agents/, .codex/, or memory/
- is a test file (path contains /tests/)
- is a config/build file (pyproject.toml, tox.ini, .gitignore, uv.lock, justfile, etc.)

Otherwise, read the diff (old_string vs new_string from tool_input, or the full new content for Write) and decide: does this change affect user-visible behavior? Specifically check for changes to:
- CLI flags or arguments → update docs/getting-started/syntax.md
- Metacommand syntax, new metacommands, or conditional tests → update docs/reference/metacommands.md
- Configuration options (INI sections/keys in config.py) → update docs/reference/configuration.md
- Export formats or exporter behavior → update docs/reference/metacommands.md (EXPORT section)
- Import formats or importer behavior → update docs/reference/metacommands.md (IMPORT section)
- Substitution variable behavior or new system variables → update docs/reference/substitution_vars.md
- Logging format or log record types → update docs/guides/logging.md
- Database connection handling or new database support → update docs/getting-started/requirements.md and docs/getting-started/syntax.md
- GUI behavior or framework support → update docs/getting-started/syntax.md (-v option) and docs/reference/configuration.md (gui_level)
- Script formatter behavior → update docs/guides/formatter.md

Internal refactors, bug fixes with no behavior change, test-only changes, and code style changes do NOT need doc updates.

If a doc update IS warranted: read the specific target doc page, and make the minimal targeted update using the same formatting conventions (mkdocs-material definition lists with `:   ` syntax, `{ #anchor_id }` for anchors, no `<a id>` HTML anchors, no `\:` escaped colons). Do not rewrite sections that are still accurate.
